summary:
RestoreWorld is an interactive territorial intelligence system designed to guide safe, data-driven green reconstruction in post-conflict and post-disaster regions using open NASA Earth observation data.We developed a four-layer analytical platform fusing thermal (MODIS LST/Albedo, Landsat 8/9), biological (MODIS EVI/Evapotranspiration), hydrological (SMAP soil moisture and GPM IMERG rainfall), and disturbance (NASA FIRMS) datasets over a uniform hexagonal grid. Using deseasonalized time series, Change-Point Detection, Sen’s Slope, and the Mann-Kendall test ($p < 0.05$) benchmarked against intact neighboring control cells, RestoreWorld answers what is changing, where, how fast, and whether it is statistically significant—capturing opposite interconnected trends such as dropping soil moisture and vegetation triggering surging surface heat.

The interface classifies territories into four actionable levels—Urban Thermal Emergency, Hydrological Flood Risk, Silent Agricultural Contamination (from drone batteries and shrapnel), and Stable Control—paired with a UXO-safe mobile field verification tool ("Time X-Ray") and automated green restoration prescriptions (urban green corridors, bioswales, and non-food phytoremediation crops).

This is critical because rebuilding blindly with concrete over damaged soil locks in lethal heat islands, flash floods, and toxic food chains. RestoreWorld turns satellite science into resilient, safe recovery.
details:
What does it do and how does it work?
RestoreWorld acts as a forensic Earth System Trend Detective for post-conflict and post-disaster territories. It transforms raw, multi-sensor NASA Earth observation datasets into actionable green reconstruction plans across a four-layer workflow:


1. Multi-Sensor Data Fusion: Over a uniform hexagonal grid, the system ingests and cross-examines four open NASA satellite layers:
◦ Thermal:MODIS (MOD11A2) and Landsat 8/9 (TIRS) for Land Surface Temperature (LST) down to 30m parcel resolution, plus MODIS (MCD43A3) for surface Albedo.
◦ Biological:MODIS (MOD13Q1) for Enhanced Vegetation Index (EVI/NDVI) and MODIS (MOD16A2) for Evapotranspiration (ET).
◦ Hydrological:NASA SMAP (surface and root-zone soil moisture) paired with GPM (IMERG) precipitation data to distinguish climatic drought from mechanical soil compaction.
◦ Disturbance Timeline:NASA FIRMS active thermal anomalies to pinpoint the exact dates of bombings, industrial fires, or acute impacts.


2. Statistical Rupture Engine: RestoreWorld removes natural seasonal cycles against a historical baseline (2000–pre-event), detects exact breakpoints aligned with FIRMS alerts, and benchmarks every suspect cell against intact neighboring control cells experiencing identical rainfall. It then calculates Sen’s Slope (rate of change) and executes the non-parametric Mann-Kendall Test (p < 0.05) to separate statistically proven environmental ruptures from random weather noise.


3. Four-Tier Tactical Prioritization: The interactive map classifies cells into Level 1 (Urban Thermal Emergency), Level 2 (Hydrological Flash-Flood Risk), Level 3 (Silent Agricultural Degradation), and Level 4 (Stable Control Reference), capturing opposite interconnected trends driven by the same disturbance (e.g., plummeting evapotranspiration and soil moisture triggering surging surface temperatures).


4. Safe Field Verification & Green Prescription: Once demining teams certify an area clear of unexploded ordnance (UXO), technicians use the mobile "Time X-Ray" split-screen module to overlay NASA’s historical anomaly layer onto live geotagged camera views. Finally, RestoreWorld generates mandatory ecological prescriptions prior to rebuilding—such as urban green corridors, bioswales, and non-food phytoremediation crops.


What benefits does it have?
• Eliminates Statistical False Alarms: By enforcing a strict p < 0.05 Mann-Kendall significance filter and control-cell benchmarking, decision-makers do not waste scarce reconstruction funds on temporary meteorological fluctuations.
• Bridges the Technical Gap: Translates complex satellite formats and non-parametric statistics into two seamless operational views—a color-coded tactical triage map for urban planners and field brigades, and an auditable statistical dossier (Sen's slope, p-values, Before/After series, and CSV exports) for environmental engineers.
• Protects Field Personnel: Integrates a mandatory safety gate ensuring mobile ground-truthing is strictly restricted to UXO-cleared zones.


What is the intended impact of the project?
Rebuilding war-torn or disaster-hit regions blindly with concrete over compacted, deforested, or contaminated soil locks in long-term environmental hazards. RestoreWorld prevents cities from cementing lethal urban heat islands, stops downstream flash floods caused by lost soil infiltration, and protects public health by quarantining agricultural land contaminated by heavy metals before food crops are replanted. Built entirely on global, open-access NASA APIs, it is scalable to any post-conflict or post-disaster region worldwide—serving reconstruction ministries, municipal planners, humanitarian NGOs, and agricultural recovery agencies.


What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?
• NASA Open Datasets: MODIS (MOD11A2, MCD43A3, MOD13Q1, MOD16A2), Landsat 8/9 TIRS, NASA SMAP, NASA GPM IMERG, and NASA FIRMS.
• Programming Language & Core Libraries: Python 3, utilizing pandas and numpy for time-series deseasonalization and hexagonal grid aggregation, scipy and pymannkendall for Change-Point Detection, Sen’s Slope, and Mann-Kendall significance testing, and plotly for interactive geospatial mapping and multi-axis time-series visualization.
• Web Application & Deployment: Built with Streamlit for rapid interactive prototyping and mobile-responsive field simulation, version-controlled on GitHub, and deployed on Streamlit Community Cloud.
• Hardware: Standard consumer laptops for statistical modeling and web development, plus mobile smartphones for testing the responsive "Time X-Ray" field interface.


How is your project creative?


• Detecting "Silent" Agricultural Contamination (Level 3): Beyond obvious burn scars, RestoreWorld identifies a hidden threat of modern conflict: farmlands with no major fire alerts (FIRMS ≈ 0) that nonetheless suffer a subtle, statistically significant drop in vegetation vigor (EVI). By cross-referencing intact control plots, the system flags suspected heavy-metal micro-contamination from drone batteries (lithium, copper, nickel) and shrapnel (lead), prescribing non-food phytoremediation crops (such as industrial sunflowers or hemp) to extract toxins before resuming food production.
• Opposite-Trend Forensic Pairing: Instead of viewing variables in isolation, our engine explicitly links inverse trends triggered by the same physical trauma—proving how destroying vegetation and compacting soil simultaneously collapses water retention while spiking surface heat.
• "Time X-Ray" Augmented Field View: Connects orbital history directly with ground-level inspection by splitting the mobile screen between live camera capture and NASA's historical thermal/vegetation anomaly layers.


What factors did your team consider?
• Scientific Rigor vs. Usability: We balanced strict statistical validity (deseasonalization, control-cell normalization, and p < 0.05 significance thresholds) with intuitive visual triage so non-scientists can act immediately.
• Spatial & Temporal Resolution Trade-offs: We combined MODIS (20+ years of continuous historical baseline) with Landsat 8/9 (30m parcel-level precision) so planners get both long-term climate context and street/field-level granularity.
• Human Safety & Ethics: Recognizing that post-conflict zones contain unexploded ordnance, we designed the ground-verification workflow around strict UXO clearance gating and prioritized food-chain safety through phytoremediation quarantines.
• Global Replicability & Open Science: Every dataset and software library used is 100% open-source and globally available, ensuring zero licensing barriers for humanitarian and public-sector deployment.
